care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Thank you for reaching out! I'll help you determine your Child Benefit eligibility. Let me ask you some questions to assess your situation.

First, I need to know about the child you're claiming for:

**How old is your child?**

This is important because eligibility rules differ based on age:
- Under 16: Generally qualify automatically (subject to other conditions)
- 16-19: May qualify if in approved education or training
- 20 or over: Generally not eligible

## Eligibility Assessment for Alex

**Status: Cannot be determined without additional information** ⚠️

### The Situation

Based on what you've told me, Alex meets several important requirements for Child Benefit:

✅ Alex is 16 years old and in approved education  
✅ Alex lives with you  
✅ Alex works less than 24 hours per week

**However, there's one critical piece of information needed:**

❓ **Does Alex receive any benefits in their own right?** Specifically:
- Universal Credit
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Income Support

### Why This Matters

If Alex is **NOT** receiving any of these benefits in their own name, then **you would be ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit.

If Alex **IS** receiving any of these benefits in their own right, then **you would be INELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Next Steps

**You need to check:**
1. Whether Alex has claimed or is receiving Universal Credit, ESA, or Income Support in their own name
2. Note: Benefits you receive for your household don't count - only benefits Alex receives personally

**Once you know the answer:**
- If Alex is NOT receiving these benefits → You can apply for Child Benefit
- If Alex IS receiving these benefits → You cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex

**To apply or get more information:**
- Apply online: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit
- Call the Child Benefit helpline: 0300 200 3100

Please check Alex's benefit status and feel free to come back if you have any other questions!
